transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-21
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 38 min
Attendees: Samira Patel (Redwood AE), Diego Marquez (Redwood SE), Hannah Li (Redwood Product), Jordan Hayes (LumenWare - Head of ML), Priya Nair (LumenWare - Security Architect), Ben Cooper (LumenWare - Platform), Aisha Khan (LumenWare - Compliance)

Summary (auto): Quick console + API walkthrough of data handling guardrails: redaction, retention toggles, request storage modes (ephemeral vs store), audit logs, and encryption/KMS integration. Demo focused on how to enforce low-retention test pilot while preserving auditability for compliance.

00:00 Samira: okay everyone, thanks for joining um we'll keep this tight, we're gonna show the console and a few API examples for the data controls you asked about. jordan and team — is the goal to validate you can run a pilot with minimal retention and still meet SOC2/ISO needs?
00:18 Jordan: yeah that's right, like we want to make sure PII doesn't persist in logs and we can toggle storage per environment. Also need to understand the encryption options and who can see what in the audit logs.
00:30 Priya: and to add, we have EU residency constraints for some workloads so we need exportable proof of deletion for DSARs.
:36 Diego: great, that's what we'll cover. quick outline: console toggles for request storage, automatic redaction pipeline, masking rules, audit logs and export, KMS keys, and a sample API param set for ephemeral flows. then we'll run a small demo creating a retention policy.
01:02 Hannah: quick note on terminology: when I say "request storage" I'm referring to the server-side option that decides whether we persist request payloads/tokenized traces for debugging and quality. some teams call it "logging" and others call it "request store" — apologies for mix of terms if the transcript says "rack store" or similar.
01:20 Priya: yep that's helpful.
01:26 Diego: i'm gonna share my screen — bear with me. logging... ok i see the LumenWare tenant, thanks ben for provision.
01:36 Ben: yep i just added the test project and a service account. i gave the redwood-demo role.
01:42 Diego: perfect. first up, the Console -> Data Controls section. top-level toggle: Request Storage Mode with three options: "Ephemeral (no storage)", "Short retention (X days)", "Full retention (audit)". that first one sets data to not be written to persistent store and keeps only in-flight memory on the runtime. important note: ephemeral still writes minimal request metadata to the audit index for rate-limiting and billing (we store hashes not raw text).
02:12 Priya: can you show what hashed vs raw looks like in the UI? sometimes those are confusing to auditors.
02:18 Diego: yes. switching to the audit logs view. so here's an example entry when ephemeral is on — you see a timestamp, request id, model used, token count, and a hash blob. it intentionally doesn't include the prompt text. older logs here show full text when retention policy is set to full.
02:36 Jordan: how does the hash work for DSAR verification? can we compute the same hash to prove something?
02:42 Hannah: good question. we support HMAC with a tenant-specific salt so you can verify presence without revealing content. it's not reversible. for DSARs we provide an audit export that shows which requests were deleted and the associated hashes so teams can correlate without exposing PII.
03:01 Aisha: that is promising. need the exact proof language for our auditors though.
03:08 Diego: sure we'll add that to the SOC pack.
03:11 Samira: Diego, could you demo an API call that sets ephemeral on a per-request basis? jordan asked about toggles per environment and per-route.
03:21 Diego: absolutely. switching to terminal — example curl:

curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>'
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json'
  -d '{"model":"rw-base-2","input":"customer PII test","request_options": {"storage": "ephemeral", "redaction": "auto"}}'

03:52 Jordan: nice — so this parameter overrides the tenant default?
03:56 Diego: yes, per-request overrides are supported for hosted and dedicated. in private deployments you can enable the same API surface but you manage policy enforcement. there's also a per-route policy in the console so platform teams can lock down overrides for production routes.
04:20 Priya: what's the "redaction": "auto" flow? is it regex-based or ML-based? we need to know false positive/negative behavior.
04:30 Hannah: it uses a layered pipeline — first a quick regex pass for common structured PII (emails, ssn-ish patterns), then an ML model trained on redaction examples to catch contextual PII. you can supply custom rules too. the console shows redaction preview and false positive rate historically for a given rule set.
04:51 Ben: can we push our custom regex rules via API? we want infra-as-code.
04:56 Diego: yes the config is represented as YAML and exposes an API (we'll share examples). the Console shows the rule editor for quick changes, but infra teams should manage through config-as-code to avoid drift.
05:12 Jordan: sounds good. i want to double-check the privacy pipeline doesn't impact latency too much. for real-time features latency matters.
05:21 Diego: understood — redaction runs inline but is optimized: regex in the edge, ML model in a lightweight container with batching. in our benchmarks we add ~15-30ms median for common flows; worst-case depends on cape- I mean cache misses and sequence length.
05:39 Jordan: cache misses? you mean KV cache?
05:41 Diego: yeah, kv cache — sorry, typed as "kayvee" earlier in docs — the KV cache warm path reduces repeated prefix compute so redaction + inference are amortized.
05:50 Priya: about key mgmt — we need customer-managed keys. do you support external KMS or HSM?
05:58 Hannah: yes. we support AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault, and bring-your-own HSM via KMIP. encryption-at-rest for request stores can be tied to your KMS, and you can rotate keys on schedule. rotation does not require re-encrypting historical blobs for audit hashes since we store hashes separately.
06:20 Aisha: and what about export of audit logs for regulators — can we push logs to our SIEM?
06:25 Diego: yes, audit exports can be pushed to S3, BigQuery, or a webhook for SIEM ingestion. there's also a streaming export for high-throughput customers.
06:34 Ben: if we choose Short retention like 7 days, is deletion immediate at 7-day boundary or eventual? we need proof of deletion windows.
06:42 Diego: retention enforcement runs a deletion job every 24 hours for short retention buckets; for compliance we also provide a deletion certificate file for the batch that shows which objects were removed. for immediate deletion requests we support manual purge via API which returns a job id and a deletion certificate when finished.
07:03 Priya: ok good. show me the manual purge flow.
07:07 Diego: switching back to the terminal, example:

curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/admin/purge
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <admin-token>'
  -d '{"project_id":"lw-test","filter":"request_id in (..)", "reason":"DSAR compliance"}'

07:28 Diego: response returns {"job_id":"purge-20260521-1234"} and later you can GET /admin/purge/:job_id to get status and a deletion-certificate URL.
07:41 Priya: is the deletion certificate signed? we may need signed attestation.
07:45 Hannah: yes it's signed by Redwood's platform key and includes timestamps, object IDs, and the tenant-provided reason. we'll include verifier instructions in the pack.
07:58 Jordan: what about traceability — if we set ephemeral and later need to investigate a production issue, is there any path to recover request content?
08:07 Diego: ephemeral mode intentionally discards content; we only retain non-reversible hashes and minimal metadata. for production debugging we recommend short-retention with strict RBAC around logs — you can restrict access to specific roles and require an approval workflow in the Console to unlock full-text viewing.
08:25 Ben: can that unlock be integrated with our approval system? we use Okta SSO and approve flows via an internal ticketing system.
08:31 Diego: yes, we have SSO/SAML integrations and an approvals webhook so you can require a ticket id before full-text is surfaced. the UI will show the linked ticket and who approved.
08:44 Priya: perfect. are those approval events all in the audit log?
08:48 Hannah: yes, approval events are first-class audit entries with user id, approver, timestamp, and reason. they're retained independently of request store retention to preserve evidentiary trail, configurable to your compliance needs.
09:03 Jordan: on the API side — can we tag requests with custom labels so we can route some through dedicated pools? e.g., eu-finance -> dedicated eu pool with data residency.
09:12 Diego: yep, you can pass metadata tags in request_options and then routing policies can map tags to pools or model variants. the console also has a routing rules engine for this.
09:23 Samira: quick pause — priya asked earlier about EU residency, do you need us to show the private deployment packaging or just the region controls?
09:31 Priya: region controls are fine for now, but we'll likely evaluate private for the highest risk workloads.
09:36 Diego: show region selector — under deployment -> regions, you can pin routes to eu-west-1-only and enforce that any request with tag eu_* routes there. we also support on-prem appliance for air-gapped needs.
09:49 Ben: when using private, do we still get Redwood console features like audit exports?
09:53 Hannah: yes, private ships a control-plane connector that pushes telemetry metadata to your chosen sink; you can keep the UI on Redwood or run the control plane behind your VPC.
10:04 Jordan: can you walk us through a short demo of a retention policy change and then issuing a purge and audit cert?
10:09 Diego: sure — i'm going to toggle the project's request storage to "Short retention: 7 days". clicking save... policy updated. now i'll run a create request with storage=full so we can see an object that will be deleted.
10:24 Diego runs sample request (audio shows keyboard)
10:30 Diego: done — request id 7f9c. now i will trigger manual purge for requests older than 0 days in the demo bucket to simulate deletion. submitting purge job... job id purge-20260521-demo.
10:46 Diego: job completed — pulling certificate: cert-url: https://s3.redwood-demo/purge-cert/purge-20260521-demo.json (note: link is demo). certificate includes signed timestamp and object ids.
10:57 Priya: good to see. when we run the pilot we'll want that automated to our SIEM.
11:02 Diego: noted.
11:05 Jordan: a few questions on the redaction accuracy — can we run evals on our sample prompt sets? we want regression alerts when model or rule changes increase leakage.
11:15 Hannah: yes, Redwood Optimize ties into your eval sets: you upload labeled examples and Optimize runs continuous checks after model rollouts and rule updates, sends alerts for regressions, and can block rollouts with gating if configured.
11:28 Ben: do those evals run on your infra? any data leaving our environment?
11:33 Samira: for pilot we can run Optimize in a mode where evals run in your private deployment or using an encrypted processing enclave. we provide both options.
11:44 Priya: who has access to Optimize results? restrict to roles?
11:48 Hannah: results access is RBAC-controlled; you can restrict to specific groups and optionally redact test inputs in the UI while still surfacing metrics.
11:58 Jordan: what about billing impact for these features — e.g., redaction ML + optimize eval runs — how are they priced?
12:05 Samira: generally redaction compute is included in hosted tiers up to a token threshold; heavy custom ML redaction or large eval batches may be billed as add-ons. we'll share a pricing snapshot.
12:16 Jordan: okay send that.
12:19 Diego: one more quick thing: you asked about programmatic enforcement of retention per route — here's an example policy snippet we recommend in infra-as-code:

policy:
  name: lw-short-retain
  match: tag == "pilot" and env == "staging"
  actions:
    set_request_storage: "short:7d"
    require_approval: true

12:45 Ben: that looks like something we can push through our Terraform pipeline.
12:49 Priya: regarding encrypted search — sometimes we want redaction but still be able to search metadata for fraud detection. what's exposed in metadata?
12:57 Diego: metadata includes non-textual attributes — token counts, model, tags, timestamp, user id, and a search index on allowed metadata fields. full-text search is only available when retention allows. for hashed content we provide a PHI-safe index by pre-hashing searchable fields if you opt-in.
13:17 Aisha: for compliance we need to show the chain-of-custody for data access. does Redwood log who requested a full-text unlock and what they saw?
13:25 Hannah: yes every view is audited — the audit entry records the approver, viewer, timestamp, request id and reason. we can export those events for your auditors.
13:36 Jordan: any gotchas for using ephemeral in automation? for example retries or async jobs where text may be needed for debugging.
13:44 Diego: great point — retries that require original input need storage. we recommend a pattern: set ephemeral for live traffic, but route failed async tasks to a short-retention queue where data is encrypted with your KMS. also implement structured error payloads to reduce need for raw text in debugging.
14:05 Ben: can we also get alerts if the system sees unexpected PII patterns slipping through? like an ML-based leak detector?
14:12 Hannah: yes, Optimize includes a leakage detector that scans a percentage of kept requests and flags candidates. you can set thresholds to trigger alerts or auto-redaction re-run.
14:23 Priya: would that scanning count against our retention billing or is it free?
14:27 Samira: scanning is billed as part of Optimize evaluation minutes; we'll include estimations in the follow-up.
14:34 Jordan: i'm curious about the audit log retention being independent — if we keep audit events longer than request store, do those events contain any text? we need audit logs to be PII-free but still useful.
14:45 Diego: audit logs do not contain raw text unless you explicitly enable that for certain roles. by default they store hashed references and metadata. you can configure additional fields but that's typically reserved for internal debugging with strict RBAC.
14:57 Ben: what exactly is included in the deletion certificate? it helps to see an example field list.
15:03 Diego: certificate contains job_id, tenant_id, deletion_timestamp, list_of_object_ids (s3 keys masked), signing_key_id, signature, and reason. for legal teams we can also provide a mapped CSV with request ids and deletion timestamps.
15:20 Aisha: ok we'll want that CSV format.
15:23 Samira: noted. I'll include it in the pack.
15:26 Jordan: couple final things — incident response and forensic: if there's suspected data exfiltration we might need to re-run redaction on historical data if retention allowed it. is that supported?
15:38 Hannah: if you have the objects retained under short/full retention, you can run a post-hoc redaction job that scans and rewrites objects with new redaction rules; the job creates an new signed certificate. for ephemeral there is nothing to re-run.
15:52 Priya: do you have rate limits or quota concerns for these background jobs? we might run large surveys.
15:58 Diego: background jobs are rate-limited; large jobs are scheduled and can be prioritized for dedicated customers. for the pilot we can allocate a higher throughput window.
16:10 Jordan: ok looks good. let's talk timelines: if we start pilot next week, who do we need from Redwood and from us?
16:18 Samira: from Redwood: AE + SE support to onboard, a product contact for rule templates, and weekly check-ins. from LumenWare: platform eng to provision roles, security to review SOC pack, and one ML tester to provide eval sets.
16:32 Ben: we can assign that.
16:35 Priya: a final question — does Redwood support deletion requests initiated by end-users (DSAR) via API? we have to link to our customer portal.
16:43 Diego: yes, we expose that API and can forward DSARs to a purge job; you can also expose the SDK method to your portal to trigger and poll for completion.
16:55 Aisha: what's the estimated time to complete a DSAR purge for a single user — like if they have 200 requests across a project?
17:02 Diego: typically purges for a single user are minutes to an hour depending on index size; we'll provide more precise numbers once we run against your pilot dataset.
17:13 Samira: great. i'm going to recap next steps. we'll send SOC 2 + ISO docs, the API snippets for ephemeral and purge, and the sample infra-as-code policies. diego will prepare a short demo checklist for the pilot and ben will give us the IAM details. jordan, can you confirm pilot scope by Friday?
17:31 Jordan: yes we'll confirm scope and the eval set.
17:34 Samira: perfect. any final questions?
17:37 Priya: none from me, thanks.
17:39 Ben: good.
17:40 Aisha: thanks all.
17:42 Samira: thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the pack.

End of transcript.
